Learning Mechanics open research area finder

Place each research area in a cube by how hard it is, how much it would matter, and how much theory already exists for it. Then compare your picture with everyone else's.

Local demo mode: data lives in this browser, and the community is made up of demo users. Reset demo data

How it works

Pick a research area from the dropdown. It appears in the cube, and you drag it into place: drag the dot to set Difficulty and Impact, and drag the arrows above and below it to set Existing theory. Drag anywhere else to rotate the cube. Changes save as you go, and you can come back to any area later.

The two aggregate views show where others put each area. Global Aggregate covers everyone else who has responded, and Learning Mechanics Group Aggregate covers only members of the Learning Mechanics group. Click an average to see the individual responses behind it. In either view you can leave a comment on your whole placement or on a single area. Comments aren't shown individually; instead Claude writes a daily summary of what people have said.

The axes

Difficulty
How hard real progress is, from trivial to near impossible.
Impact
How much solving it would matter, from no impact to field-defining.
Existing theory
How much predictive theory already explains the area, from none to established.

Each edge of the cube runs from one extreme to the other, and the centre is the midpoint of all three axes. Positions are relative, so there are no numbers. Your GitHub username appears next to your points.
